notes:
The Business Privilege Tax passes the inclusion test on the Department of Revenue's own wording: it is levied "for the privilege of being organized under the laws of Alabama or doing business in Alabama" and it "remains due every registered year until the entity is legally dissolved/withdrawn" whether or not the entity trades. It is a levy on being registered, not on income and not on a filing event.
minimumAnnualUsd is 0 and it is a published zero, not an absent minimum. For taxable years beginning after 2023-12-31 (Act 2022-252) the tax is fully exempt where the calculated amount is $100 or less, and the 2026 Form PPT prints the same rule on the computation line: "If $100 or less, STOP. You do not have a filing requirement. Do not submit return." So an Alabama LLC below that threshold pays nothing and files nothing. The $100 figure that reads like a minimum is the ceiling of the exemption, not a floor.
The rate bands and the ceiling are recorded, from the section the agency page itself cites. Section 40-14A-22(b) sets the rate at $0.25 per $1,000 of net worth at the bottom and $1.75 per $1,000 above $2,500,000, with the band chosen by the taxpayer's taxable income rather than by its net worth; subsection (d) caps the tax at $15,000 for an ordinary taxpayer, with a higher ceiling for financial institution groups and insurers that this record does not carry because no schema field holds a maximum. The section's own amendment history ends at Act 2022-252, which is the act that created the exemption, so the text read here is the text that produced the $0 minimum.
firstYearExemption is false, and the statute is blunter than the agency page about why: the tax accrues on the date the entity is organized, incorporated, registered or qualifies to do business, not from the following January. Alabama gives a new entity the opposite of a waiver, and Form BPT-IN is due within two and one-half months of organizing, an extra return the later years do not require. The $100-or-less exemption does reach BPT-IN by its own terms, but it is an exemption by amount and not by year, which is a different fact from the one this field carries.
collectedWithAnnualReport is false. Root states.json carries annual_report_fee 0 for Alabama because the Secretary of State no longer requires an annual report, so this tax is not the payment root already counts and a total-cost consumer must add it rather than choose between them. Read the form title with care before changing this: Form PPT is called "Alabama Business Privilege Tax Return and Annual Report", but that Annual Report is the Department of Revenue's own attachment, not the Secretary of State filing root's figure refers to.
The Electing Pass-Through Entity election reaches a multi-member LLC as a Subchapter K entity; a single-member LLC is disregarded and has no entity-level return to elect on. topRatePercent 5 is the top band of the individual rate schedule, which is also the rate the composite return uses for nonresident members.
